:::{#def-epl}
#### Expected prediction loss at a covariate value

The **expected prediction loss at $\predvar$**
of a [fitting procedure](#def-fitting-procedure) $\fitproc$
at training-set size $\nobs$
is the expected [loss](#def-observation-loss) $\obsloss{*}$
of its prediction $\fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}$ for a new outcome $\newoutvar$ with $\newpredvar = \predvar$,
averaged over random [training sets](#def-training-set) $\trainset$ of $\nobs$ observations
drawn independently of $(\newpredvar, \newoutvar)$,
and over $\newoutvar$:

$$
\epl{\fitproc}{\nobs}{\predvar} \eqdef \E{\obsloss{*} \mid \newpredvar = \predvar}.
$$ {#eq-epl}

:::

:::{#rem-epl-generalization-error}
#### The expected prediction loss and the generalization error

The [generalization error](#def-generalization-error) $\generr_{\trainset}$
holds the training set fixed and averages the loss over new covariate values too.
The expected prediction loss at $\predvar$ averages over training sets as well,
and holds the covariate value fixed.
Neither is the [test error](#def-test-error):
the test error is an average over a finite test set,
so it estimates the generalization error without equalling it.

:::
